title: Some features of high-temperature superconductivity on flat bands
authors: V. R. Shaginyan, A. Z. Msezane, S. A. Artamonov
abstract: In this letter, we examine how the presence of flat band leads to the formation of a high-temperature superconductor even in the case of repulsive pairing interactions. We also show that in the case of flat bands, the high-temperature superconducting state deforms the flat band, tilting it and making the effective mass finite. As a result, neither the superfluid weight nor the supercurrent disappear. Our results are in good agreement with experimental data.
summary: This work theoretically explains how high-temperature superconductivity can emerge in systems with flat energy bands, even when repulsive interactions are dominant. It proposes a 'self-help' mechanism where the superconducting pairing itself deforms the band structure, ensuring that supercurrents and superfluid weight remain finite. The findings align well with experimental observations in heavy-fermion and high-$T_c$ superconductors.
main_problem: The paper investigates how flat bands can induce high-temperature superconductivity, even when repulsive pairing interactions are present.
main_result: Superconductivity in the presence of flat bands is sustained by a 'self-help' mechanism where the superconducting state deforms the band, preventing the superfluid weight and supercurrent from vanishing.
method: The analysis adapts standard BCS theory formalism to the specific physical context of flat bands formed in strongly correlated Fermi systems.
model_or_system: The system involves strongly correlated Fermi gases exhibiting topological fermion condensation quantum phase transitions (FCQPT), leading to localized states forming flat bands at the chemical potential.
key_observables: Critical temperature ($T_c$), superfluid weight ($D_s$), effective mass ($M^*$), superconducting gap ($\Delta$), and Fermi velocity ($V_F$).
important_parameters: Repulsive pairing interaction strength ($\lambda_0 > 0$); the condition for flat bands ($\varepsilon(p) - \mu = 0$).
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the superconducting state actively modifies the band structure (tilting it) to maintain finite superfluid properties, overcoming initial theoretical predictions of collapse.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows experimental data for $V_F$ vs. $T_c$ in graphene and $\Delta$ vs. integrated LDOS ($\propto 1/V_F$) for high-$T_c$ superconductors, both consistent with the derived theoretical relationship.
paper_structure: The paper first addresses the apparent contradiction where flat bands suggest zero superfluid weight; it then introduces the 'self-help' mechanism via BCS formalism to show finite $D_s$; finally, it discusses how this framework explains high-$T_c$ behavior even with repulsive interactions and relates findings to experimental data.
why_interesting: The concept of a superconducting state actively modifying its own underlying electronic structure (band deformation) is a rich topic relevant to understanding emergent order parameters in complex quantum materials.
